 ▶ Zeynep Sönmez defeats Maya Joint at Osaka 2026 – Round 1 
 1079 views • 1d Zeynep Sönmez overturned a slow start to defeat Maya Joint 3-6, 6-4, 6-3 in 2h15min on the Osaka hard courts. The Turkish 63rd-ranked player absorbed the pressure of a match between two in-form competitors and secured progression to Round 2.
The result extends Sönmez’s recent hard-court resilience. Before this match, she had beaten Anastasia Zakharova and Sinja Kraus in qualifying, although she had lost to Yulia Putintseva in three sets the previous week. Her victory over Joint adds another competitive win after a demanding stretch against ranked opposition.
Joint, ranked 90th, had entered with two qualifying wins in Osaka, defeating Kyoka Okamura and Kayla Day. Her wider hard-court record showed strong upside, including victories over Liudmila Samsonova, Sorana Cîrstea, Yuliia Starodubtseva and Lanlana Tararudee, but also several narrow losses in extended three-set matches.
The Australian’s opening set reflected that confidence, yet Sönmez changed the match’s direction in the second. Joint’s recent results suggest she remains capable of challenging higher-ranked players, while Sönmez’s ability to recover against a direct ranking rival strengthens her position in the Osaka draw.
